title: Kitchen Renovation Price: UK Cost Guide
description: Find out the typical kitchen renovation price in the UK, including labour, materials, design changes and the factors that can increase your final quote.

blocks.text: If you are researching kitchen renovation price, the first thing to know is that there is no single figure that applies to every home. A straightforward replacement of doors and worktops costs very differently from a full renovation involving new units, rewiring, plumbing, flooring or structural changes. As a rough UK guide, a kitchen renovation may typically cost from around £3,000 for a limited refresh to £30,000 or more for a larger, higher-spec project. Every property and specification is different, so these figures are for early budgeting only; request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

items: Cosmetic refresh: as a rough guide, typically around £3,000–£8,000, which may include painting, new handles, doors, selected appliances, worktops or splashbacks.
Standard kitchen replacement: as a rough guide, typically around £8,000–£18,000, often including new cabinets, worktops, appliances and installation, with limited changes to the existing layout.
Full renovation: as a rough guide, typically around £18,000–£30,000 or more, where the project includes new services, flooring, tiling, lighting, higher-spec finishes or a substantial layout change.
Large or high-spec kitchen project: typically £30,000 and above, particularly where there are bespoke cabinets, extensive building work, an extension or expensive appliances.

blocks.text: These ranges can overlap because the size of the kitchen is only one part of the calculation. A compact kitchen with bespoke cabinetry and extensive electrical work may cost more than a larger room using standard units and keeping the existing layout. Location can also affect labour rates and availability, so prices may differ between contractors. Every project differs, and a free, no-obligation quote is the best way to establish an accurate price.

How labour affects the kitchen renovation price

Labour can account for a significant part of the budget. A basic installation may involve assembling and securing units, fitting worktops, installing appliances and making final adjustments. A more involved renovation could require several trades, including cabinet installation, plumbing, electrical work, tiling, flooring, plastering and decorating. As a rough guide, labour and installation might typically total around £3,000–£8,000 for a kitchen, but this can be lower for a simple fitting job or considerably higher where the room needs preparation and several trades are involved. Every project differs, so request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
What should be included in a fitting quote?

Ask whether the quote covers removing and disposing of the old kitchen, preparing walls and floors, fitting cabinets, cutting worktops, connecting appliances, plumbing, electrical work, tiling and making good. Some quotes show only the cabinet installation price, while others cover a more complete renovation. Comparing like for like is important: a cheaper initial figure may not include waste removal, plastering, flooring or final decoration.

Materials are a major variable in the budget. Standard flat-pack or modular cabinets can be more economical, while rigid, painted, solid-wood or bespoke cabinetry may cost more. Worktops also vary widely: laminate can be a lower-cost option, while timber, quartz, granite and other engineered surfaces may require a larger allowance. Handles, sinks, taps, splashbacks and lighting can appear minor individually but add up across the room.

items: Worktop material, thickness, joins and cut-outs for sinks or hobs.
The number and specification of ovens, hobs, extractor fans, dishwashers and refrigeration appliances.
Sink, tap, waste-disposal and water-filtration choices.
Tiles, flooring, paint, lighting and decorative finishes.
Delivery charges, specialist fabrication and removal of packaging or old materials.

blocks.text: Design changes that can increase the final quote

Keeping the sink, cooker and dishwasher in their existing positions can help control costs because the plumbing, waste pipes and electrical supplies may need less alteration. Moving these points can involve opening floors or walls, extending services and carrying out additional testing and making good. Changing a kitchen from a single-wall layout to an L-shaped or island arrangement may also require new flooring, more lighting and different worktop fabrication.

items: Moving water or waste connections, especially where falls and access are limited.
Adding new circuits, sockets, lighting or extractor ventilation.
Removing walls, widening doorways or installing structural supports.
Repairing damp, uneven floors, damaged plaster or outdated wiring discovered during preparation.
Adding an island, breakfast bar, utility area or pantry storage.
Replacing windows, doors or radiators as part of the redesign.
Choosing bespoke storage, integrated appliances or specialist worktops.

blocks.text: Getting a more accurate kitchen renovation quote

Before requesting prices, measure the room and note the position of doors, windows, radiators, pipes, sockets and appliances. A simple plan, photographs and a list of preferred materials will help a contractor understand the scope. Decide whether you want a cosmetic update, a like-for-like replacement or a new layout. You can then compare [kitchen fitting in Watford](/kitchen-fitting-watford) with the specific work you need rather than comparing headline installation prices.

It is sensible to request an itemised quote showing labour, cabinets, worktops, appliances, plumbing, electrical work, tiling, flooring, waste removal and any building work separately. Check whether VAT is included, how unforeseen repairs are handled, what is excluded and when payment stages are due. Consider setting aside a contingency for unforeseen work in an older property, with the appropriate amount depending on its condition and the level of investigation completed before work starts.

If hidden issues are found, ask for a written explanation and revised cost before approving additional work. This gives you a clearer budget and can reduce the risk of unexpected costs during installation.

faq.q: What is the average kitchen renovation price in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough UK guide, a kitchen renovation may typically cost around £3,000–£8,000 for a refresh, £8,000–£18,000 for a standard replacement, or £18,000–£30,000 or more for a comprehensive renovation. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: How much does it cost to fit a new kitchen?
faq.a: As a rough guide, a straightforward kitchen fitting job may typically cost around £3,000–£8,000 for labour and installation, although the amount varies with kitchen size, preparation, cabinet design, worktops, appliances and the number of trades required. Every project differs, so request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to renovate a kitchen or replace it?
faq.a: A renovation that keeps the existing layout and reuses sound units can be cheaper than a full replacement. However, replacing damaged cabinets or outdated services may provide better value than repeatedly repairing them.

faq.q: What increases the cost of a kitchen renovation?
faq.a: Common cost increases include moving plumbing or electrics, removing walls, repairing floors or plaster, choosing bespoke cabinets or premium worktops, adding an island, upgrading appliances and discovering hidden problems in an older property.

faq.q: How can I get an accurate kitchen renovation quote?
faq.a: Provide room measurements, photographs, a basic layout and your preferred appliances and finishes. Request an itemised quote that clearly separates labour, materials, services, building work, waste removal, VAT and exclusions.
